land.text: 'Sergius IV of Naples gave the town and vicinity of Aversa as a county to Ranulf' (County of Aversa); Cliopatria's 1034 shape is that county

predecessors.note: The Norman state begins as a fief of the Duchy of Naples; the lands taken later come from the Byzantine Empire (Apulia, Calabria, Bari), the Emirate of Sicily, the Principality of Salerno and the Lombards of Capua and Benevento.

land.text: the whole Norman realm of Roger II (Sicily, Calabria, Apulia and the duchy lands), crowned king at Palermo on Christmas Day 1130; Capua and Naples are not yet in it

successors.note: The Kingdom of Sicily is the same Hauteville realm under a royal crown; the colour agent may keep the colour (identity.family italy) or assign a new one.

capitals.name: Aversa
capitals.note: Seat of Ranulf's county; the Aversa page gives no capital as such.

capitals.name: Melfi
capitals.note: 'the capital was moved from Melfi to Salerno' in 1078 (Duchy of Apulia and Calabria).

capitals.name: Salerno
capitals.note: 'Salerno remained the capital of this southern Italian political entity for half a century (from 1078 to 1130)' (B). The County of Sicily page gives Palermo as the capital of the county, moved there in 1112 (C).

capitals.name: Palermo
capitals.note: Reading of two pages: Roger II inherited the mainland duchy in 1127 (C, E) and the Sicilian capital was Palermo (C); B keeps Salerno as the duchy's capital to 1130.

rulers.name: Robert Guiscard
rulers.title: Duke of Apulia and Calabria
rulers.note: B's succession table: 'Robert Guiscard 1059-1085'. The earlier counts (Ranulf of Aversa from 1030, William Iron Arm of Apulia from 1042/43) have no reign years on the pages opened.

rulers.name: Roger II
rulers.title: Duke of Apulia and Calabria, Count of Sicily
rulers.note: B: 'Roger II 1127-1134'; he was crowned King of Sicily on 25 December 1130 (E), which ends this state and begins the Kingdom of Sicily.

correction.text: the town and vicinity of Aversa, a county given to Ranulf by Sergius IV of Naples in 1030

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first Norman Italy shape starts in 1034, but 'In 1030, the first Norman foothold in the Mezzogiorno was created' and 'Sergius IV of Naples gave the town and vicinity of Aversa as a county to Ranulf' (the Norman conquest page: 'In early 1030 Sergius gave Ranulf the County of Aversa as a fief'). The 1034 shape (120 km2, Aversa only) is reused for 1030-1033.

120 km2 around Aversa for 1034-1039; the page gives 'the town and vicinity of Aversa' and no extent. Ranulf's 1038 invasion of Capua (Norman conquest page) is in the ledger only; no page opened says how long Capua was held. No infobox area on any page opened, so the area check could not be made.

correction.text: unchanged shape, valid 1040-1042 only (the Aversa lands)

keyframe_review.note: The 1,249 km2 Aversa-Capua shape is right for 1040-1042; from 1043 the County of Apulia was founded ('a Norman state founded by William of Hauteville in 1043', composed of 'Gargano, Capitanata, Apulia, Vulture'), which Cliopatria draws only from 1046. See the new keyframe norman-italy_1043. The shape itself is unchanged and holds 1040-1042. correction.text: the Aversa lands and the County of Apulia: Gargano, Capitanata, Apulia, Vulture, and most of Campania, without Byzantine Bari

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1043-1045: the Aversa lands plus the Apulian county. B: 'a Norman state founded by William of Hauteville in 1043' and 'composed of the territories of Gargano, Capitanata, Apulia, Vulture, and most of Campania'; the Norman conquest page has the Melfi council of September 1042 where 'William was acknowledged as the Norman leader in Apulia', and a defeat at Taranto in 1045. The block is Cliopatria's 1046 shape taken back three years, without Bari, which stayed Byzantine until April 1071.

correction.text: Cliopatria shape without Bari, which stayed Byzantine until April 1071

keyframe_review.note: 24,721 km2 for 1046-1055. The block matches B's 'Gargano, Capitanata, Apulia, Vulture, and most of Campania', but Cliopatria puts 10 of the 13 cells of Bari province inside it while the Norman conquest page says 'the city Bari surrendered in April 1071, ending the Byzantine presence in southern Italy'; Bari and its coast are removed until 1071. The Benevento and Molise cells in the shape (7 and 11 cells) overlap Cliopatria's Duchy of Benevento row and are left as drawn: the page's account of Benevento is contradictory (Civitate 1053, captured Leo IX 'imprisoned in Benevento (which had surrendered)', and Drogo conquering Benevento for the Empire in 1053).

correction.text: Cliopatria shape without Bari, which stayed Byzantine until April 1071

keyframe_review.note: 15,527 km2 for 1056-1065: Cliopatria drops the Aversa-Caserta lands and Molise, and has no Calabria. The Aversa page: 'In 1058, Richard conquered the Principality of Capua' and 'thereafter the counts of Aversa were, more importantly, princes of Capua', so Aversa and Capua leave this state in 1058 (ledger); the shape is two years early for Aversa. Bari stays outside until April 1071. Calabria is added from 1060 (see norman-italy_1060). Holds 1056-1059.

union.text: Cliopatria shape without Bari, which stayed Byzantine until April 1071

correction.text: the Apulian block without Byzantine Bari, plus Calabria after the capture of Reggio in 1060

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1060-1065: 'Reggio Calabria, the capital of the tagma of Calabria, was captured by Robert Guiscard in 1060'. Cliopatria shows no Calabria until its 1066 shape (Reggio and Cosenza provinces inside); the Calabrian part of the 1066 shape is added from 1060 to the 1056 shape. The page dates the capture of Reggio, not that of the rest of Calabria, so the extent is a reading.

correction.text: Cliopatria shape without Bari, which stayed Byzantine until April 1071

keyframe_review.note: 40,769 km2 for 1066-1071: Apulia, Calabria and the first Sicilian ground (Messina 5 of 12 cells, 1 of Catania's). The Norman conquest page: 'Robert and Roger first invaded Sicily in May 1061, crossing from Reggio di Calabria and besieging Messina'; the County of Sicily page: 'In 1061 the first permanent Norman conquest' (Messina). Bari (11 of its 13 cells inside the shape) fell only in April 1071; it is removed for 1066-1070 and counted from 1071. The pages do not date Otranto, Brindisi or Taranto, which Cliopatria also includes; left as drawn (unverified: page budget).

44,902 km2 for 1072-1076: adds the Palermo country (Palermo province 10 of 16 cells). 'The city of Palermo was entered by the Normans on 7 January 1072.' Bari is inside from 1071 and the shape holds; Salerno is added from 1077 (see norman-italy_1077).

correction.text: the Norman duchy and the Principality of Salerno after its conquest in 1076-1077

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1077-1084: Salerno joins. 'On 13 December 1076, the city submitted' and 'the citadel, which fell in May 1077' (A); 'Salerno was conquered in 1077 by the Normans, and these territories were added to the Duchy of Apulia and Calabria' (B). Cliopatria keeps a Principality of Salerno row to 1084 (5,329 km2) and gives the lands to Norman Italy only in 1085; seven years late against the pages.

correction.text: unchanged except that the Aversa-Capua block (Caserta province) is the Principality of Capua's, not this state's

keyframe_review.note: 77,764 km2 for 1085-1090: most of Sicily (71 of 89 cells) and the Salerno and Benevento blocks. The County of Sicily page does not cover Syracuse (1085) or Agrigento (1087); the Emirate's last row is the south-eastern corner, 1,288 km2 to 1093. 'In February 1091 the conquest of Sicily was completed when Noto fell', so the corner is Muslim until 1091. Cliopatria also puts the Caserta block (Aversa and Capua, all 10 cells) inside this state from 1085; the Aversa page makes the counts of Aversa 'princes of Capua' from 1058 and Roger II's page has the Principality of Capua still in being in 1134-1138, so the block is removed.

correction.text: all Sicily after the fall of Noto in February 1091, and Malta after the fall of Mdina

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1091-1093: 'In February 1091 the conquest of Sicily was completed when Noto fell' (C) and 'In 1091, Roger invaded Malta and subdued the walled city of Mdina' (A); the south-eastern Sicilian corner (Cliopatria's last Emirate of Sicily row, 1,288 km2) and Malta are added. C adds that the conquest of Malta 'was begun later that year' and completed in 1127, so Malta is a first hold, not final.

correction.text: unchanged except that the Caserta block (Aversa and Capua) belongs to the Principality of Capua

keyframe_review.note: 79,542 km2 for 1094-1125: Sicily whole and Malta (1 of 1 cell), Apulia and Calabria. Fits C (Sicily complete 1091) and A (Malta 1091); 3 years late against both. Again the Caserta block (Principality of Capua) is removed. The Duchy of Naples (Cliopatria row to 1138) is outside the shape, as the pages have it independent until 1137.

correction.text: unchanged except that the Caserta block (Aversa and Capua) belongs to the Principality of Capua; holds to 24 December 1130

keyframe_review.note: 79,542 km2 (identical to 1094-1125). Roger II inherited the mainland duchy in July 1127 and was crowned king at Palermo on Christmas Day 1130, so this shape holds for 1126-1130 under the Hauteville duke and count; from 25 December 1130 it belongs to the Kingdom of Sicily dossier, which carries 1130-1138. Caserta removed as in 1094.

region.text: the town and vicinity of Aversa (Cliopatria's 1034 shape, 120 km2)

ledger.note: 1030: Ranulf becomes Count of Aversa. 'Sergius IV of Naples gave the town and vicinity of Aversa as a county to Ranulf'; 'In 1030, the first Norman foothold in the Mezzogiorno was created.' The Norman conquest page: 'In early 1030 Sergius gave Ranulf the County of Aversa as a fief.' Cliopatria's first shape starts 1034.
1038: Ranulf invades Capua. 'In 1038 Ranulf invaded Capua, expanding his polity into one of the largest in southern Italy.' The page does not say how long Capua was held.

1041: the Normans fight the Byzantines for Apulia. 'On 4 May 1041 the Norman army, led by William Iron Arm, defeated the Byzantines again' (Montemaggiore); the word 'again' means earlier fighting the page does not date.

region.text: Gargano, Capitanata, Apulia, Vulture, and most of Campania; Cliopatria's 1046 shape without Bari

ledger.note: 1043: the County of Apulia is founded. 'a Norman state founded by William of Hauteville in 1043', 'composed of the territories of Gargano, Capitanata, Apulia, Vulture, and most of Campania'. The Norman conquest page puts the Melfi council, where 'William was acknowledged as the Norman leader in Apulia' and received the title of Count of Apulia from Guaimar of Salerno as his vassal, in September 1042.
1044: the conquest of Calabria begins. 'William and Guaimar began the conquest of Calabria in 1044.'
1057: Richard besieges Capua. 'When the prince of Capua died in 1057, Richard immediately besieged the comune.'

region.text: Aversa and Capua, the Drengot lands (Aversa as Cliopatria's 1034 shape)

ledger.note: 1058: Richard takes Capua and the Aversa lands leave this state. 'In 1058, Richard conquered the Principality of Capua'; 'thereafter the counts of Aversa were, more importantly, princes of Capua'. The Drengot counts of Aversa and the Hauteville dukes of Apulia are two separate Norman lines from here; Aversa and Capua are the Principality of Capua's. The Norman conquest page: 'Richard and Jordan took the princely title in 1058.'
1058: the siege of Capua ends with Richard and Jordan as princes. 'Richard and Jordan took the princely title in 1058.'

1059: the county becomes a duchy. 'It became a duchy when Robert Guiscard was raised to the rank of duke by Pope Nicholas II in 1059'; the infobox timeline reads 'Treaty of Melfi; the County becomes a Duchy'. The Norman conquest page adds that Guiscard 'made himself a papal vassal in return for the title of duke'.

region.text: Reggio Calabria, the capital of the tagma of Calabria

ledger.note: 1060: Reggio and Calabria. 'Reggio Calabria, the capital of the tagma of Calabria, was captured by Robert Guiscard in 1060.' The page names the capital; the extent to the rest of Calabria is a reading.
1060: the Calabrian contest is settled with the fall of Reggio. 'Reggio Calabria, the capital of the tagma of Calabria, was captured by Robert Guiscard in 1060.'
1061: Messina, the first permanent conquest in Sicily. 'In 1061 the first permanent Norman conquest' was made at Messina.
1061: the invasion of Sicily. 'Robert and Roger first invaded Sicily in May 1061, crossing from Reggio di Calabria and besieging Messina.'

region.text: the city Bari and the last Byzantine ground in Apulia

ledger.note: 1071: Bari surrenders. 'the city Bari surrendered in April 1071, ending the Byzantine presence in southern Italy.' The page names the city; Bari province is a reading.
1071: the Byzantine presence in southern Italy ends. 'the city Bari surrendered in April 1071, ending the Byzantine presence in southern Italy.'

1072: Palermo falls. 'The city of Palermo was entered by the Normans on 7 January 1072.' The County of Sicily page has Palermo as capital of the county, established 1071 (Britannica, which it cites, gives 1072 for the capture).

1077: Salerno. 'Salerno was conquered in 1077 by the Normans, and these territories were added to the Duchy of Apulia and Calabria.' The Norman conquest page: 'On 13 December 1076, the city submitted' and 'the citadel, which fell in May 1077'. Cliopatria keeps the Principality of Salerno to 1084.

1078: the capital moves from Melfi to Salerno. 'the capital was moved from Melfi to Salerno'; 'Salerno remained the capital of this southern Italian political entity for half a century (from 1078 to 1130)'.

1078: Guiscard is appointed to Benevento. 'In 1077 the last Lombard prince of Benevento died, and in 1078 the pope appointed Robert Guiscard to succeed him.' The page does not say how much land this was beyond the city.
1081: Guiscard gives Benevento up. 'In 1081, however, Guiscard relinquished Benevento.' The page does not say to whom; the pope who had appointed him is a reading.

region.text: the island of Sicily except the Emirate's last south-eastern corner

ledger.note: 1085: the rest of Sicily outside the south-eastern corner, as Cliopatria draws it. The County of Sicily page does not cover Syracuse (1085) or Agrigento (1087); the date and extent are those of Cliopatria's Emirate of Sicily row, which shrinks from 16,348 to 1,288 km2 in 1085. Page silent.

region.text: Malta and the walled city of Mdina

ledger.note: 1091: Malta. 'In 1091, Roger invaded Malta and subdued the walled city of Mdina.' The County of Sicily page: the conquest 'was begun later that year' and completed in 1127, when 'the Arab administration of the island was expelled'. Cliopatria draws Malta from 1094.

region.text: the Emirate's last south-eastern corner round Noto

ledger.note: 1091: Noto falls and Sicily is complete. 'In February 1091 the conquest of Sicily was completed when Noto fell.'
1091: the contest for Sicily ends. 'In February 1091 the conquest of Sicily was completed when Noto fell.'

1127: Palermo becomes the capital of the united realm. Reading of two pages: Roger II 'inherited the mainland duchy' in 1127 (C) and Palermo was his capital (C, infobox; 'the capital moved to Palermo in 1112'); B keeps Salerno as the duchy's capital to 1130.

1127: Roger II inherits the mainland duchy. 'When William II of Apulia died childless in July 1127, Roger claimed all' the Hauteville possessions on the peninsula; B: 'In 1127 the duchy passed to the count of Sicily.' The Sicilian county and the Apulian duchy are one realm from here.
1128: Honorius II invests Roger as duke. 'in August 1128 Honorius invested Roger at Benevento as Duke of Apulia.'

region.text: the whole Norman realm: Sicily, Calabria, Apulia and the duchy lands

ledger.note: 1130: Roger II is crowned king of Sicily at Palermo. 'He was crowned in Palermo on Christmas Day 1130'; the antipope Anacletus II's bull of 27 September 1130 made him king. B: 'The duchy was disestablished in 1130, when the last duke of Apulia and Calabria, Roger II, became King of Sicily.' [Reviewer eu-13-h, 2026-10-25: counterpart set to kingdom-of-sicily, the successor whose found event (December 1130) names this state.]

wars.name: Norman-Byzantine war in Apulia and Calabria
wars.outcome: Norman victory: Melfi and Apulia held from 1042-1043, Reggio taken in 1060, Bari in April 1071 'ending the Byzantine presence in southern Italy'.
wars.note: 'William was less successful in Apulia, where he was defeated in 1045 near Taranto by Argyrus'; 'William and Guaimar began the conquest of Calabria in 1044'.

wars.name: Battle of Civitate
wars.outcome: Norman victory on 18 June 1053 over 'the combined forces of the pope and the Holy Roman Empire'; 'the Normans destroyed the papal army and captured Leo IX, imprisoning him in Benevento'. The page gives no territorial change.
wars.note: The page also says Drogo conquered Benevento for the imperial crown in 1053 yet died in 1051; the page is inconsistent, so no Benevento event is recorded for 1053.

wars.name: Norman conquest of Capua
wars.outcome: Richard besieged the town in 1057 and, with Jordan, took the princely title in 1058; the counts of Aversa became princes of Capua.

wars.name: Norman conquest of Sicily
wars.outcome: Norman victory: Messina besieged May 1061, Palermo entered 7 January 1072, Noto fell in February 1091 and 'the conquest of Sicily was complete'; Malta invaded in 1091.
wars.note: Intermediate steps (Cerami 1063, Syracuse 1085, Agrigento 1087) are not on the pages opened.

wars.name: Norman conquest of the Principality of Salerno
wars.outcome: Salerno submitted on 13 December 1076 and its citadel fell in May 1077; the lands were added to the Duchy of Apulia and Calabria.

certainty.note: Every frontier of the century of conquest is approximate: the counties and the duchy grew by campaigns and fiefs, not by surveyed lines. Sicily's and Malta's coasts are natural limits.

notes: Norman Italy is a Cliopatria row named for a process (its Wikipedia title is 'Norman conquest of southern Italy', Q74011), not a single state. This dossier treats it as the Hauteville and Drengot conquest state: the County of Aversa from 1030, the County of Apulia from 1043 (Duchy of Apulia and Calabria from 1059), the County of Sicily from 1061, united under Roger II in 1127 and ending when he was crowned king in December 1130. The Kingdom of Sicily dossier carries 1130 onward; Cliopatria's Norman Italy row runs on to 1138 and the Kingdom row restarts in 1139. Cross-checks for other dossiers: (1) Principality of Capua: Cliopatria's row stops in 1065, yet the Aversa page makes the Drengot counts princes of Capua from 1058 and Roger II's page has the Principality still in being in 1134-1138; Cliopatria's Norman Italy shape swallows the Caserta block from 1085, which is removed here. (2) Principality of Salerno: the pages put the fall in 1076-77, Cliopatria's row runs to 1084. (3) Duchy of Benevento: Cliopatria's row (12,234 km2) lies almost wholly inside Norman Italy's shapes of 1046-1055 and 1085 onward; the pages say only that Guiscard held Benevento city 1078-1081. Left as drawn, flagged for the eu-13 Benevento dossier. (4) Emirate of Sicily: dossier should end its island rows in 1091 (Noto), not 1093. Pages disagree: the Norman conquest page puts William of Apulia's recognition at the Melfi council of September 1042, the Duchy page founds the county in 1043; the Norman conquest page says Guiscard was made duke 'of Sicily' at an undated moment and omits the 1059 investiture of Guiscard (it covers Richard at Melfi), the Duchy page dates it 1059. The Norman conquest page is internally inconsistent about Drogo (assassinated 1051, conquest of Benevento 1053). Not on any page opened: Cerami 1063, Otranto 1068, Syracuse 1085, Agrigento 1087, the Treaty of Mignano's terms (only Roger II's page names it, with the date 25 July 1139 derived), Honorius's 1128 Treaty of Benevento terms; William Iron Arm's reign years and the Aversa counts' dates. The infobox of none of the five pages gives an area, so the area comparison could not be made; Cliopatria's 79,542 km2 for 1094-1138 is unchecked. Vassalage: the pages make the Norman counts vassals of Guaimar of Salerno (1042), Guiscard a papal vassal from 1059, and Roger I count of Sicily under the suzerainty of the Duke of Apulia; these are not drawn as events here (the suzerain's dossier carries them). Gazetteer names the gazetteer lacks and that are used only in text or via Cliopatria's 1034 shape: Aversa, Melfi, Mdina. The cell grid is about 250 km2, so Aversa and Capua are one to three cells each.
